the surveillance duplex criteria used in our practice for stent grafts for occlusive disease do not reliably predict stent graft failure for popliteal aneurysms.

surveillance duplex ultrasonography using criteria established for stent grafts in the lower extremity occlusion population is not reliable in predicting stent graft occlusion in the popliteal artery stent graft population.
surveillance DU of stent grafts for popliteal aneurysm is not reliable for detecting stent graft failure.

the development and application of a new method of surveillance for popliteal aneurysm stent grafts.
the use of duplex ultrasound to evaluate the patency and function of stent grafts that were placed in patients with popliteal artery stenosis and aneurysm.
the evaluation of the reliability and the usefulness of duplex ultrasound in the diagnosis of stent graft failure after popliteal aneurysm repair.

the use of duplex ultrasound surveillance in patients with stent grafts for popliteal aneurysms is not recommended.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the current DU criteria for failing stent graft surveillance may not be applicable to stent graft surveillance for popliteal aneurysm treatment.
stent grafts for popliteal aneurysms are not reliable for long-term patency and should be used only in the setting of high operative risk.

The main takeaway from our work is that
DU surveillance for stent grafts for popliteal aneurysms should be interpreted with caution.
DU surveillance of stent grafts for popliteal aneurysms is likely not necessary, and that patients with popliteal aneursyms can be followed clinically without DU surveillance.
DU surveillance for popliteal stent grafts is not as reliable as it is for grafts for occlusive disease.
